card.name: Rebuttal and debunking in argumentative web text
card.fires_on: Sentence-ending periods, linking words like Furthermore or In fact, and other small words in polemic web text that denies or refutes a claim, often just after a flat denial such as 'a total lie' or 'a straw man'.

modes.label: Period after a denial
modes.description: A full stop closing a sentence that calls a claim false, ignorant or a straw man.
modes.example: That again is a straw man<<.>> The big bang theory doesn't suggest spiral

modes.label: Linking word starting a counterpoint
modes.description: A connector like Furthermore, In fact or Why opening the next point of a rebuttal.
modes.example: Nowhere in any of the Dead Sea Scrolls is anything ever said about Jesus.<< Furthermore>>, while apocryph

modes.label: Word inside a rebuttal clause
modes.description: A small word or word ending within a sentence that rejects an opposing claim.
modes.example: The decay rate he stated has been debunk<<ed>> and stated as flawed.

card.writes: It pushes toward absolute negatives such as 'none', 'never' and 'nowhere', and away from hedges such as 'somewhat' and 'slightly'.
card.plain: It marks points in an angry argument where the writer flatly denies a claim, and it favors absolute wording over hedging.
